output.brief: The gap is mostly explained by how long people have been in their current level, not by where they work. Remote hiring only opened widely in July 2024, so most remote staff are new: only 32% of remote staff are eligible for promotion under the 18-month rule, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, nomination rates (28% vs 29%), approval rates (71% vs 74%) and promotion rates (20% vs 21%) are almost the same. Remote attrition is not higher than office attrition, and the gap shows up in every job family, so neither explains it. Caveat: the eligible remote group is only 110 people, so a real difference of a few points can't be excluded. Managers' comments hint that urgent, visible work goes to nearby staff, but we have no data on that. I would not announce the three-day office rule. It rests on a headline comparison that mixes eligible and ineligible people, and it would penalise about 180 people hired on home-based contracts. Instead, put the rule on hold, report promotion rates for eligible employees only, and re-check at the FY2027 cycle. Also look at how stretch work is assigned.
